topic: Ionic and Covalent Bonds and Compound Properties
key_concepts: Chemical bonds hold atoms together in compounds
Lewis dot structures show valence electrons as dots around element symbols
The octet rule states that atoms tend to become stable with eight valence electrons
Ionic bonding involves complete transfer of valence electrons from a metal to a nonmetal
Ions are charged particles; cations are positive and anions are negative
Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points and are usually solid at room tempera
Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution but not as solids
Covalent bonding involves sharing of valence electron pairs between nonmetals
Nonpolar covalent bonds share electrons equally while polar covalent bonds share unequally
Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points and usually do not conduct electric
Ionic compound formulas are written using oxidation numbers and the crisscross method
Covalent compounds are named using prefixes such as mono-, di-, and tri- with an -ide endi
